Package neqsim.pvtsimulation.flowassurance

Class AsphalteneSolidModel

java.lang.Object
neqsim.pvtsimulation.flowassurance.AsphalteneSolidModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class AsphalteneSolidModel extends Object implements Serializable
Calibrated solid asphaltene precipitation model (Nghiem and Coombe type) on a cubic equation of state.

Precipitated asphaltene is a pure solid whose fugacity depends only on temperature and pressure. It is anchored at a measured onset point (T*, P*) of a reference oil: 

 ln f_s(T, P) = ln f_L(T*, P*) + v_s (P - P*) / (R T) - (h_s / R) (1/T - 1/T*)

where f_L is the asphaltene fugacity in the equilibrated fluid (gas and oil, no solid). Asphaltene precipitates when f_L exceeds f_s. Because the solid reference is independent of the fluid, one calibration on the host oil predicts the onset of the same oil at other pressures and of the same asphaltene in blends with other fluids (gas injection, condensate commingling).

The composition response comes from the asphaltene interaction parameters. Unlike the default (zero), they follow a size-asymmetry correlation of Chueh-Prausnitz form on the equation-of-state co-volume (b proportional to Tc/Pc): 

 k_ij = 1 - [2 (b_i b_j)^(1/6) / (b_i^(1/3) + b_j^(1/3))]^e

so small molecules (N2, CO2, methane, ethane) get large values and heavy fractions near zero. This makes light diluents raise the onset pressure, as titration and field data show. With zero interaction parameters dilution of the asphaltene dominates and the model wrongly predicts that light diluents stabilise the oil.

Calibration levels: calibrate(double, double) (one onset, solid volume from the asphaltene density), calibrateLowerOnset(double) (adds the lower onset below the bubble point and fits the solid volume), calibrateTemperature(double, double) (adds an onset at a second temperature and fits h_s), and fitKijExponent(SystemInterface, double, double, double, double) (fits e to a measured onset of a blend).

The fluid must contain exactly one component whose name contains "asphalten" (for example the database component "asphaltene" or a TBP fraction added by PedersenAsphalteneCharacterization), use a cubic equation of state with the classic mixing rule set, and be water-free. If the equation of state splits the asphaltene into a separate liquid (characterization too immiscible), isAsphalteneLiquidSplitDetected() returns true; lower the asphaltene acentric factor or interaction exponent.

References: Nghiem, L.X., Coombe, D.A. (1997). Modeling asphaltene precipitation during primary depletion. SPE Journal 2(2), 170-176. Nghiem, L.X., Hassam, M.S., Nutakki, R., George, A.E.D. (1993). Efficient modelling of asphaltene precipitation. SPE 26642.

    • fitKijExponent

      public double fitKijExponent(SystemInterface fluid, double temperature, double measuredOnsetPressure, double maximumPressure, double minimumPressure)
      Fit the interaction exponent to a measured upper onset of another fluid (for example a host-condensate blend), keeping the reference-fluid calibration. Golden-section search over [0.3, 3.5].
      Parameters:
      fluid - fluid with the measured onset (cloned)
      temperature - temperature in K
      measuredOnsetPressure - measured upper onset in bara
      maximumPressure - top of the search range in bara
      minimumPressure - bottom of the search range in bara
      Returns:
      the fitted exponent (also set on the model)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the fluid has the calibration composition and the temperature is within 0.5 K of the calibration temperature
